key_insight: A steady, spatially varying Kolmogorov flow can drive a passive nematic from stationary to periodic and irregular dynamics without velocity fluctuations or hydrodynamic feedback.
engineering_relevance: Steady patterned flows could offer a route to controlling time-dependent nematic responses without time-varying forcing.
method: Vary imposed flow strength in a planar passive-nematic model.
Characterise transitions using bifurcation and phase-space analyses.
Use two-mode and five-mode reduced-order models to identify dynamical mechanisms.
evidence_signal: The two-mode model captures periodic onset through a saddle-node infinite-period bifurcation, while the five-mode Galerkin model recovers stationary, periodic and irregular regimes.
watch_item: The model excludes velocity fluctuations and nematic feedback on the flow, so applicability to fully coupled systems remains to be established.
paper_title: Complex nematic dynamics driven by steady Kolmogorov flows
